agree.reason: The email opens with Dana's own $600K figure, shows a conservative case where the savings beat the $75K cost, and asks for a small 20-minute call, so a busy VP could plausibly reply, but nothing about IT effort would move a director who resists change.

honest.reason: The 'more than half' claim is limited to the one customer where it's true (4.1→1.9 is about 54%), and the smaller 2.8→2.2 result is shown; the only omission is that just two of six customers have shared numbers.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the full five-site cost ($75K) and checks it against a conservative 20% case ($120K), which is close to the real 21% result; it doesn't give the upside (about $320K at a 54% cut) or the net figure.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is implied: keep losing about $600K a year. It is tied to her own number, but the email never says outright that doing nothing keeps that cost.

qualification.reason: 'Not every site sees a drop that big' is an honest hedge, but it gives her nothing to check: no pilot site, no target rate, no date and no consequence if results fall short.

objections.reason: 'Doesn't replace your WMS, sits on top of it, about three weeks' speaks to the IT worry, but it doesn't say how little IT work is needed or that the recent rollout stays as it is, and it raises no needless objections.

fit.reason: It is a short cold email in short paragraphs that read easily on a phone, with a specific subject line and one clear ask, as the brief asked.
